title: FedVS: Towards Federated Vector Similarity Search with Filters

problem.claim: The task is to identify the k nearest neighbors to a query object among vectors satisfying an attribute filter constraint.

gap.claim: Most existing solutions focus on single-sourced data and overlook vector retrieval across federated datasets.

contributions.claim: The paper introduces federated vector similarity search with filters for privacy-preserving vector retrieval over multisourced data held by mutually untrusted providers.
FedVS is a privacy-preserving framework using indexing and pruning based on a Trusted Execution Environment.
The paper provides theoretical analysis covering complexity, security, and approximation guarantees for recall.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report deploying their solution over real-world vector databases and conducting extensive experiments.
The authors report that their solution outperforms state-of-the-art methods in effectiveness and efficiency.

narrative_sequence.summary: Vectors represent unstructured data through embeddings and associated attributes, and large-scale similarity search has attracted substantial interest.
Filtered similarity search seeks the k nearest neighbors satisfying an attribute constraint.
Existing solutions generally target single-sourced data and do not address retrieval across federated datasets.
The paper defines the federated filtered-search problem and proposes FedVS with privacy-preserving indexing and pruning based on TEE.
The paper presents theoretical guarantees, real-world vector-database deployment, extensive experiments, and reported effectiveness and efficiency improvements.

source_observation.claim: Federated vector retrieval must account for privacy, recall, latency, and communication cost across mutually untrusted providers.

interpretation.claim: Distributed retrieval designs should evaluate both security and systems-level tradeoffs rather than optimizing search quality alone.

application.claim: When designing cross-provider vector search, combine privacy mechanisms with indexing and pruning, and analyze their effects on recall, complexity, latency, and communication.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish that the reported approach generalizes to all federated vector databases or deployment settings.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the datasets, baselines, metrics, or numerical experimental results.
The abstract does not describe the threat model or the concrete security and approximation guarantees.
The abstract does not quantify recall, latency, communication cost, or effectiveness and efficiency improvements.
